problem: Pretrained vision-language models used in VLN are trained on web data and are insensitive to indoor scenes. They also ignore the sequence-level context between sub-instructions along a path, so alignment is mostly out-of-context.
motivation: The distribution gap between web pretraining data and indoor VLN environments hurts scene understanding. VLN is sequential decision-making, so the agent must align ordered sub-instructions with sub-paths. Prompt learning is cheap and can inject both kinds of knowledge into a pretrained model.
key_idea: A two-stage prompt-based pretraining: learn deep visual prompts on a CLIP-labelled indoor image dataset (indoor-aware), then use hand-designed hard context prompts (count, sequential, individual, overall) with contrastive learning to align sub-instructions and sub-paths (context-aware).
insight: Both stages help on their own and are complementary (Table 3: R2R val-unseen SR 62.75 baseline, 65.05 with visual prompts only, 64.84 with context prompts only, 65.60 with both). A control that aligns only sub-instructions and sub-paths (L_sub, no context prompts) gives little gain (SR 63.14), and less than L_cnt alone on val-unseen. This shows the gain comes from sequence-level context prompting and not from extra exposure to the domain. Adding L_ind and L_ove to L_cnt improves results step by step (SR 63.37, 64.26, 64.84).
method: Indoor dataset generation: CLIP zero-shot matches Matterport3D images against 'A photo of a {object}' templates (object and room labels) and takes the top-scoring label, giving about 1000 indoor image-text pairs.

Deep visual prompt tuning: 10 learnable prompt tokens are inserted at the first n layers of PREVALENT's visual encoder. The backbone is frozen, and only the prompts and an MLP classification head are trained with cross-entropy for 20 epochs.
Sub-instruction/sub-path generation: FGR2R splits R2R instructions at 'and', commas and periods, and pairs each piece with its sub-path.

Hard context prompts: four hand-written text templates. The count prompt is 'This instruction contains {M} actions'. The sequential prompt is 'this is the {seq_i} action'. The individual prompt is '{seq_i}, perform the action {a_i}'. The overall prompt concatenates all individual prompts.

Contrastive fine-grained alignment: viewpoint embeddings from the prompted visual encoder and sequential prompt embeddings go through the cross-modal encoder. A learnable count token is added. A symmetric KL-divergence contrastive loss is applied to sub-path/individual, mean-pooled overall, and count-token/count-prompt pairs. Total loss = λ1·L_ove + λ2·L_cnt + ΣL_ind, with λ1=0.5 and λ2=0.1.
Downstream fine-tuning: the pretrained model initialises a RecBERT agent, which is fine-tuned on R2R (with PREVALENT augmented data, 300k iterations) and REVERIE (200k iterations).

setting.backbone: RecBERT agent initialised from PREVALENT, with deep visual prompts and context-prompt contrastive pretraining (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: About 1000 CLIP-labelled Matterport3D indoor image-text pairs; R2R sub-instruction/sub-path pairs (FGR2R); R2R train plus PREVALENT augmented data; REVERIE train
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB viewpoint features on the Matterport3D connectivity graph, plus language instruction

results: On R2R, PANDA reaches 66 SR / 60 SPL on val-unseen and 64 SR / 59 SPL on test-unseen, beating the RecBERT (PREVALENT) baseline (63/57 val-unseen; 63/57 test-unseen) and ADAPT, ProbES and SEvol. On REVERIE, it improves RGS and RGSPL over RecBERT on val-unseen (20.76/17.74 vs 18.77/15.27), but RecBERT has higher test SR/SPL (29.61/23.99 vs 27.81/20.89).
limitations: Gains are modest (1-3 points), and on REVERIE test-unseen SR/SPL are worse than the RecBERT baseline.
The indoor dataset is small (about 1000 CLIP-labelled pairs), and the labels are noisy, generated automatically.
Only R2R and REVERIE are evaluated, with a single backbone (PREVALENT), and the hand-designed prompt templates and sub-instruction splitting rules are heuristic.
